checks.lead: Urracá or Ubarragá Maniá Tigrí (died 1531) was an Ngäbe chieftain or cacique in the region of present-day Panama who fought effectively against the Spanish conquistadors. The Spaniards captured Urracá when he met them to discuss a peace treaty, caged him, and sent him to the Caribbean port of Nombre de Dios, intending to send him to Spain. He escaped, and for "the next eleven years", with his band of men, conducted guerrilla warfare against the conquistadors, living and hiding in the hills, ultimately dying from natural causes in 1531. Urracá commenced one of the first "sustained guerrilla wars in Latin America[n]" history and is remembered as el caudillo amerindio de Veragua (the Amerindian leader of Veragua) and adversary of the Spanish Empire, the great resistance leader of Panama. He has been honored by his image on the centesimo, the smallest-denomination coin of Panama.
